subject: Multi-stage notification windows & subprocessor sequencing for incident notices
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rivera <dpo@finservco.com>; security+incidents@finservco.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-stage notification windows & subprocessor sequencing for incident notices

Hi Maya / FinServe team,

Thanks for taking this call last week. To help finalize the onboarding DPA language, we want to put forward a concrete proposal for how Redwood would handle incident notifications that trigger subprocessor involvement and any necessary cross-border exports. The goal is to be operationally explicit so legal teams can sign off without ambiguity.

High-level proposal (attached: proposed-notify-flow.pdf):
- Initial alert: Redwood notifies the named customer security and DPO contacts within 6 hours of identifying a potential incident that could reasonably affect FinServe data. This is a fast, high-level escalation (no PII breakdown).
- Scoping window: Within 48 hours we will provide a scoped impact summary (types of data potentially affected, subsystems, estimated record counts) and a proposed evidence snapshot plan.
- Evidence handover: Forensic snapshot delivery or a secure export is completed within 72 hours of mutual scope agreement where technically feasible; if export requires third-party subprocessors or cross-border transfer approvals, Redwood will aim to hand off a preliminary, limited export within 7 days while coordinating additional approvals.

Questions we want clarified from your side so we can bake them into the DPA amendment:
1) Does FinServe require an explicit signed export authorization before Redwood initiates any subprocessor request that results in cross-border movement?
2) Do you want Redwood to maintain a signed manifest for any subprocessor data pull (recommended) and what minimum fields are required on that manifest?
3) Are there country-specific acceleration windows (e.g., EU regulator expectations) that would shorten the 72h evidence handover?

We’re trying to balance speed (so you can triage) with legal controls around exports and chain-of-custody. Ben, can you confirm the feasibility of the 72h evidence handover for typical incidents (small/medium/large)? Kimberly, if that timeline deviates from our DPA template, call out the exact clause text we should propose.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Security & Escalations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-notify-flow.pdf (diagram), forensic-export-ops.md (ops runbook reference)

From: Maya Rivera <dpo@finservco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security+incidents@finservco.com
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Multi-stage notification windows & subprocessor sequencing for incident notices

Jordan — thanks for the clear proposal and the diagram. Two immediate items from FinServe legal/privacy: 

1) Export authorization: We do require an explicit written authorization before any export of European personal data to be initiated by a vendor, unless that export is within the scope of an existing data transfer mechanism (e.g., SCCs + approved org mapping). A preliminary, encrypted snapshot may be acceptable if it remains within EU storage until authorization.

2) Manifest: Yes, we need a signed manifest for any subprocessor pull that includes: scope id, time window, data descriptors (pseudonymized counts are okay initially), origin region, list of subprocessors involved, and an audit digest (hash).

Also: please confirm whether Redwood's subprocessors list is current in the DPA schedule; if a new subprocessor will be engaged to perform an export, FinServe requires 5 business days' notice unless the DPA permits emergency access.

We can accept the 6h initial alert and a 48h scoping note. The 72h evidence handover is tight for larger exports involving long KV caches or cross-region transfer; can you document the fallbacks for when the 72h window is not technically possible?

I'll loop Legal to prepare suggested DPA text.

— Maya Rivera
DPO, FinServeCo

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>; Maya Rivera <dpo@finservco.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-stage notification windows & subprocessor sequencing for incident notices

On Mon, Apr 26, 2027 at 11:08 AM Maya Rivera <dpo@finservco.com> wrote:
> Jordan — thanks for the clear proposal and the diagram. Two immediate items ...

Quick operational notes from the runtime side to inform the DPA wording:
- For most incidents where affected surface area is limited (single model instance, constrained user set), we can produce a scoped forensic snapshot (metadata + encrypted token-level samples) within 24-48 hours.
- Large-scale incidents (multi-tenant load, long sequence KV cache across dozens of GPUs) can require more time due to reconstructing token streams and verifying chain-of-custody — realistic window is 5-10 business days for full exports if cross-border redaction or legal uplift is required.
- Suggested mechanism for handover: encrypted S3 presigned + a signed manifest (as Maya requested). We can also offer a managed transfer to a FinServe-controlled bucket inside your AWS account (recommended for cross-border control).
- If a subprocessor (e.g., forensic vendor) must be engaged, we will submit a formal subprocessor request; where the DPA allows emergency access, we will still provide notice and manifest within 24 hours of the pull.

I've uploaded a brief ops runbook for this flow: forensic-export-ops.md (link in thread). We'll add a short appendix describing the cases that expand the 72h window.

— Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Rivera <dpo@finservco.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-stage notification windows & subprocessor sequencing for incident notices

Jordan / team — drafting guidance from Legal. A few contract-level changes we should propose to FinServe so obligations match operational reality: 

1) Notify vs. Handover: Keep the 6h initial notification commitment in the DPA. For evidence handover, propose a "target" of 72 hours and an explicit exception clause: "where technical reconstruction or cross-border approvals are required, the Provider shall use best efforts and shall provide updated timelines no later than 72 hours after initial notification." That preserves SLA intent but acknowledges complexity.

2) Export Authorization: Insert an export authorization workflow: customer confirms export via a one-click approval link or signed email within 5 business days; where the customer does not respond and an urgent regulatory deadline applies, Redwood may proceed under the DPA emergency access clause after documented escalation.

3) Subprocessor manifest and chain-of-custody: Redwood will provide a machine-readable manifest (CSV) and a signed hash of the artifact. We should also commit to retaining forensic snapshots for 90 days unless customer requests deletion earlier.

4) Subprocessor notice period: Keep FinServe's request of 5 business days for non-emergency onboarding. For emergency forensic pulls, allow immediate engagement but require post-fact notice within 24 hours.

I'm attaching a DPA amendment draft with tracked changes (dpa-amendment-draft.docx). Ben, please add the technical appendix language that lists the specific conditions that push full export beyond 72 hours.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Rivera <dpo@finservco.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>; Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security+incidents@finservco.com
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 16:32:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Multi-stage notification windows & subprocessor sequencing for incident notices

Kimberly / Jordan — appreciate the specificity. FinServe is comfortable moving forward on the hybrid approach you describe:

- 6 hour initial alert (no change)
- 48 hour scoped impact summary (no change)
- 72 hour target evidence handover; if the provider cannot meet the target, they must issue an updated timeline and provide a secure preliminary snapshot held in-region until export authorization is granted
- Manifest and hash required for all subprocessor pulls; 5 business days' notice for standard subprocessor onboarding, emergency pulls allowed with 24h post-notification

Next steps: FinServe Legal will review your dpa-amendment-draft.docx and propose language for the export authorization checkbox and the manifest fields. Can we coordinate a 30-minute sync with Legal + Security tomorrow to align on the exact CSV manifest columns and the method for delivering signed hashes? I'll create a HubSpot task (HS-782145) and add my team.

Thanks — Maya
DPO, FinServeCo
